drivingQuestion: Is the baraita's censure of one who sounds his voice in prayer absolute?
outcomeNote: A ruling and two successive restrictions of its scope; nothing is attacked or defended.

segments.he: הַמַּשְׁמִיעַ קוֹלוֹ בִּתְפִלָּתוֹ הֲרֵי זֶה מִקְּטַנֵּי אֲמָנָה. אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: לֹא שָׁנוּ, אֶלָּא שֶׁיָּכוֹל לְכַוֵּון אֶת לִבּוֹ בְּלַחַשׁ, אֲבָל אֵין יָכוֹל לְכַוֵּון אֶת לִבּוֹ בְּלַחַשׁ — מוּתָּר. וְהָנֵי מִילֵּי, בְּיָחִיד, אֲבָל בְּצִיבּוּר — אָתֵי לְמִיטְרַד צִיבּוּרָא.
segments.en: It was taught in a baraita: «One who sounds his voice during his» Amida «prayer is among those of little faith. Rav Huna said: This was only taught» in a case «where one is able to focus his heart» while praying silently, «but» if he «is unable to focus his heart» while praying «silently, he is permitted» to sound his voice. «This applies only to» one praying «alone,» but when he is praying «in a congregation» his voice «will come to disturb the congregation» and it is prohibited.

moves.cueHe: המשמיע קולו בתפלתו הרי זה מקטני אמנה
moves.summary: the clause of the baraita cited in the preceding unit (berakhot.24b.2) is taken up as a lemma
moves.about: the clause of the baraita about one who lets his voice be heard during the Amida is taken up for comment

moves.cueHe: אמר רב הונא: לא שנו אלא
moves.summary: Rav Huna restricts the censure to one who can concentrate while praying silently
moves.about: the baraita's censure applies only to one who can concentrate while praying silently; one who cannot may raise his voice

moves.summary: the leniency is confined to one praying alone, lest he disturb the congregation
moves.about: Rav Huna's leniency holds only for one praying alone, since in a congregation his voice would disturb the others
